findings.summary: EXAMPLES-003: The remote examples hard-code service/device names and never check whether `indigo_connect_server()` succeeded before waiting forever and later disconnecting `server`. findings.summary: EXAMPLES-004: Image-saving examples call `fopen()`, `fwrite()`, and `fclose()` without checking the file handle or write count. findings.title: EXAMPLES-005: The executable-driver examples model abrupt child-process cleanup with `SIGKILL` and `exit()` from the client detach callback, and they do not handle `execl()` failure in
findings.summary: EXAMPLES-005: The executable-driver examples model abrupt child-process cleanup with `SIGKILL` and `exit()` from the client detach callback, and they do not handle `execl()` failure in the child. `client.c` also leaves the adapter attached/released only by process exit. As examples, these teach fragile lifecycle handling. Prefer graceful detach/release/stop flow, report child exec failure, close unused pipe ends in both processes, and terminate the child only from normal shutdown code. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: LIB-013: The device is published into `devices[]` and the bus mutex released *before* `device->attach()` runs, so there is a window in which a device is globally visible with `DEV
findings.summary: LIB-013: The device is published into `devices[]` and the bus mutex released *before* `device->attach()` runs, so there is a window in which a device is globally visible with `DEVICE_CONTEXT == NULL`. A client enumerating in that window reaches the half-attached device and trips `assert(DEVICE_CONTEXT != NULL)` in `indigo_rotator_enumerate_properties` (`indigo_rotator_driver.c:176`); every class-level enumerate has the same assertion. Reproduced with `test_rotator_lunatico_simulator`, whose port devices are attached from an async handler while the test enumerates: `Assertion failed: (DEVICE_CONTEXT != NULL)`, SIGABRT. Not fixed. Two shapes were considered. Holding the mutex across `attach()` does **not** self-deadlock - `bus_mutex` is `PTHREAD_RECURSIVE_MUTEX_INITIALIZER` and `device_mutex`/`client_mutex` are both `#define`s of it, so a driver's `attach()` re-entering `indigo_define_property()` on the same thread is fine - but it would lock the whole bus while arbitrary driver code runs and inv [Full legacy statement in the linked report.] Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: LINUXDRV-001: PWM change handlers ignore failed `*_pwm_get()` calls, then compute frequency or duty from `period` initialized to zero
findings.summary: LINUXDRV-001: PWM change handlers ignore failed `*_pwm_get()` calls, then compute frequency or duty from `period` initialized to zero. If the PWM sysfs node disappears, permission is denied, or a read fails, this can divide by zero or push nonsensical PWM values while still updating the property as successful. Check the read result, set the changed property to `INDIGO_ALERT_STATE`, and return before doing math or writes. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: LINUXDRV-002: PWM sysfs reads parse buffers with `atoi()` without adding a terminating NUL after `read()`
findings.summary: LINUXDRV-002: PWM sysfs reads parse buffers with `atoi()` without adding a terminating NUL after `read()`. sysfs does not append NUL bytes, so parsing can read stale stack data past the bytes returned. Capture the read length, reject full-buffer reads, append `buf[n] = '\0'`, and use `strtol()` with validation. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: LINUXDRV-003: GPIO/PWM export and unexport helpers return on the first failure without rolling back or continuing cleanup
findings.summary: LINUXDRV-003: GPIO/PWM export and unexport helpers return on the first failure without rolling back or continuing cleanup. A partial connect failure can leave some GPIOs/PWMs exported, and a disconnect can stop after one unexport error while leaving the rest of the pins exported. Track successfully exported resources during connect and perform best-effort cleanup of all resources on failure and disconnect. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: LINUXDRV-004: `relay_mutex` and `port_mutex` are initialized but never destroyed before the private data is freed
findings.summary: LINUXDRV-004: `relay_mutex` and `port_mutex` are initialized but never destroyed before the private data is freed. This is unlikely to affect a single-process normal shutdown, but repeated driver load/unload cycles leak pthread mutex resources and complicate sanitizers. Destroy both mutexes during detach/delete after timers are cancelled and no callbacks can use them. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: LINUXDRV-005: If custom property allocation fails after `indigo_aux_attach()` has already succeeded, `aux_attach()` returns `INDIGO_FAILED` without releasing any properties allocated b
findings.summary: LINUXDRV-005: If custom property allocation fails after `indigo_aux_attach()` has already succeeded, `aux_attach()` returns `INDIGO_FAILED` without releasing any properties allocated before the failed allocation and without detaching the base AUX context. Add a single cleanup path that releases partially initialized properties, destroys initialized mutexes, and calls `indigo_aux_detach()`. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: OPTDRV-001: Andor initialization allocates `private_data` and `device`, locks `driver_mutex`, then breaks out of the camera loop when `Initialize()` fails without unlocking the mutex
findings.summary: OPTDRV-001: Andor initialization allocates `private_data` and `device`, locks `driver_mutex`, then breaks out of the camera loop when `Initialize()` fails without unlocking the mutex or freeing the just-allocated objects. A missing or invalid SDK path can leave the global mutex permanently locked and leak the partially constructed device. Use a cleanup path that unlocks the mutex, frees partial allocations, and continues or aborts cleanly. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: OPTDRV-002: Andor shutdown destroys the static global `driver_mutex` inside the per-device loop after using it for the current device
findings.summary: OPTDRV-002: Andor shutdown destroys the static global `driver_mutex` inside the per-device loop after using it for the current device. With multiple cameras, the next iteration locks a destroyed mutex; after one shutdown/init cycle, future SDK operations can also use an invalid mutex. Do not destroy this static process-lifetime mutex per camera. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: OPTDRV-003: Raspberry Pi exposure completion can block forever
findings.summary: OPTDRV-003: Raspberry Pi exposure completion can block forever. `exposure_timer_callback()` polls `IsAnyRequestComplete()` with no timeout while `state` never changes, and then `ReadFrame()` waits on `m_cv` with no cancellation/timeout. If libcamera drops a completion, a request was never queued, or the camera is stopped during the wait, the INDIGO timer callback can hang and leave exposure properties busy. Add a bounded wait and fail the exposure with cleanup. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: OPTDRV-004: Raspberry Pi exposure startup sets image and exposure properties to `INDIGO_BUSY_STATE`, but if `StartExposure()` fails it only logs the error
findings.summary: OPTDRV-004: Raspberry Pi exposure startup sets image and exposure properties to `INDIGO_BUSY_STATE`, but if `StartExposure()` fails it only logs the error. No property is moved to `INDIGO_ALERT_STATE`, no failure cleanup runs, and no client update reports completion/failure. Report the failed start through `CCD_EXPOSURE_PROPERTY` and image upload properties before returning. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: OPTDRV-005: The Raspberry Pi driver copies unbounded external strings into fixed buffers: `LIBCAMERA_LOG_LEVELS` into `previousSDKLogLevel[64]`, and libcamera camera names into `name
findings.summary: OPTDRV-005: The Raspberry Pi driver copies unbounded external strings into fixed buffers: `LIBCAMERA_LOG_LEVELS` into `previousSDKLogLevel[64]`, and libcamera camera names into `name[128]` via `strcat()`. Long environment values or camera names can overflow stack/static buffers. Use bounded copies or `std::string` construction followed by `snprintf()` into INDIGO name buffers. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: OPTDRV-006: `mmap()` results are stored without checking for `MAP_FAILED`
findings.summary: OPTDRV-006: `mmap()` results are stored without checking for `MAP_FAILED`. A failed mapping is later read as image memory in `ReadFrame()` and later passed to `munmap()`, which can crash or corrupt exposure output under memory pressure or invalid buffer FDs. Check each mapping, unwind any mappings made for the request, and fail `StartCapture()` cleanly. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.summary: OPTDRV-007: The Raspberry Pi connection path appends mode items for every supported format/size without checking the allocated capacity of `CCD_MODE_PROPERTY` or resizing it. findings.summary: OPTDRV-008: `X_CCD_ADVANCED_PROPERTY` is deleted on disconnect but not released or nulled, then reconnect defines the stale pointer before overwriting it with a newly allocated property. Detach only releases it while connected. This leaks the advanced property on disconnect/reconnect and leaves stale property state reachable. Release and null the property on disconnect, and allocate before defining it on connect. findings.title: TEST-010: `cooler_individual_failures` and `Guiding and abort during long exposure then reacquire` fail intermittently, and only under full-suite load: 11 standalone runs of the bi
findings.summary: TEST-010: `cooler_individual_failures` and `Guiding and abort during long exposure then reacquire` fail intermittently, and only under full-suite load: 11 standalone runs of the binary were clean while the two full `make test` runs hit one each. `wait_state()` samples the property's current state every 10 ms, so a state the driver publishes and then replaces between two polls is missed; the serial harness avoids this by recording a revision per state (`property_state_revisions` in `simulator_test_common.h`). findings.summary: TESTS-001: The GPS script labels `UTC_TIME`, `GPS_STATUS`, and `GPS_ADVANCED` as optional, but tests them with `test_property_exists()`, which records failures when absent. findings.title: TESTS-002: Framework commands expand `$INDIGO_PROP_TOOL` and `$REMOTE_SERVER` unquoted and usually pipe output through `grep` without `pipefail`
findings.summary: TESTS-002: Framework commands expand `$INDIGO_PROP_TOOL` and `$REMOTE_SERVER` unquoted and usually pipe output through `grep` without `pipefail`. findings.summary: TESTS-003: Most compliance scripts save `WAS_CONNECTED` from `test_connection_battery()` and then ignore it, always disconnecting the target device at the end. findings.title: TESTS-004: Abort-motion tests assume a long-running move is still `BUSY` after a fixed two-second sleep
findings.summary: TESTS-004: Abort-motion tests assume a long-running move is still `BUSY` after a fixed two-second sleep. Fast devices can finish before abort is sent and fail the required `BUSY -> OK` abort transition even though the driver is valid; slow devices can also leave a background `indigo_prop_tool` process running in the rotator test. Use a generated long move known to remain busy, wait until the motion property reports `BUSY`, send abort immediately, and wait/reap any background helper process. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TESTS-005: Property and range parsing is based on unanchored regular expressions over human-readable `indigo_prop_tool` output
findings.summary: TESTS-005: Property and range parsing is based on unanchored regular expressions over human-readable `indigo_prop_tool` output. Item checks can match substrings from unrelated items, and range extraction takes the first bracketed expression from all output instead of the requested item line. Parse exact item names from structured tool output if available, or filter to the exact property item with fixed-string matching before extracting state, values, and ranges. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.summary: TESTS-006: Framework documentation is out of sync with the implementation: `print_test_summary()` now counts skipped tests, but the early example and prose still describe only passed/failed counts. findings.title: TOOLS-001: The property parsers build `sscanf()` formats with field widths equal to destination buffer sizes, which still leaves room for a terminating NUL beyond the array
findings.summary: TOOLS-001: The property parsers build `sscanf()` formats with field widths equal to destination buffer sizes, which still leaves room for a terminating NUL beyond the array. The remote-server parser also uses `%[^:]:%s` with no widths for `hostname[255]` and `port_str[100]`. Exact-size or long command-line arguments can overflow stack/global buffers before validation. Use bounded widths of `sizeof(buffer) - 1`, check `item_count < MAX_ITEMS` before appending parsed items, and reject overlong fields. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-002: `indigo_raw_crop` trusts the RAW header and ROI dimensions
findings.summary: TOOLS-002: `indigo_raw_crop` trusts the RAW header and ROI dimensions. It does not validate the header read, RAW signature, positive crop width/height, multiplication overflow, allocation success, or payload read size. A truncated or crafted RAW file, or a crop like `0,0,-1,10`, can drive undersized allocation and out-of-bounds reads/writes. Validate the header and type, compute byte counts with overflow-checked `size_t`, require `width > 0 && height > 0`, and fail if reads or allocations are incomplete. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-003: `fits_to_raw` does not check CFITSIO status after reading image parameters or pixels, accepts any non-8-bit FITS image as 16-bit output, and allocates image buffers from
findings.summary: TOOLS-003: `fits_to_raw` does not check CFITSIO status after reading image parameters or pixels, accepts any non-8-bit FITS image as 16-bit output, and allocates image buffers from unchecked axis multiplication. Bad or unsupported FITS inputs can produce corrupt RAW output or memory faults. Check `status` after every FITS call, explicitly accept only supported `bitpix` values, validate `naxis/naxes`, and verify allocation/write results. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-004: The RAW-to-FITS utility has fragile file handling
findings.summary: TOOLS-004: The RAW-to-FITS utility has fragile file handling. `write()` is treated as a one-shot full write, input allocation/reallocation is unchecked, `fseek()`/`ftell()` and `fread()` failures are ignored, and each glob pattern is evaluated repeatedly in separate `glob()` calls before `globfree()`. This can mis-handle partial I/O, leave uninitialized data in conversions, or leak glob state. Use checked `size_t` file sizes, loop until all output bytes are written, call `glob()` once per pattern, and check all I/O results. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-005: Metadata tools copy paths into fixed buffers or pass paths through a shell command unsafely
findings.summary: TOOLS-005: Metadata tools copy paths into fixed buffers or pass paths through a shell command unsafely. `indigo_driver_metadata` uses `strcpy()` from arbitrary CLI arguments into `name[128]`; `indigo_metadata_extractor` builds `clang -E %s` for `popen()` without quoting and then dereferences `pipe` without checking for failure. Long paths can overflow, and specially named driver paths can change shell behavior. Use `snprintf()`/length checks and fork/exec-style invocation or strict shell quoting plus `popen()` failure checks. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-006: The generator assumes allocations, reallocations, file redirects, and path copies always succeed
findings.summary: TOOLS-006: The generator assumes allocations, reallocations, file redirects, and path copies always succeed. `allocate()` immediately `memset()`s a possibly NULL allocation, `realloc()` results overwrite the only pointer, `freopen()` results are ignored, and `strcpy(source_file, definition_file)` can overflow `PATH_MAX`. Failures can crash the generator, read from the wrong stream, or emit partial files. Add checked allocation helpers, temporary pointers for `realloc()`, bounded path copies, and explicit `freopen()` error handling before generating output. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-007: The repair tools read whole files and then inspect or rewrite fixed offsets without first proving the file is large enough, and they do not check write results
findings.summary: TOOLS-007: The repair tools read whole files and then inspect or rewrite fixed offsets without first proving the file is large enough, and they do not check write results. A small input can make `fix_fits` read past the loaded buffer at offset 5760, while `fix_xisf` can rewrite from `data + 2880` even when the file is shorter. Validate minimum sizes before fixed-offset access and check every `fwrite()`/`fputc()` result before reporting success. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: TOOLS-008: The tools build target produces `indigo_drivers`, `indigo_driver_metadata`, and `indigo_scan_drivers`, but `install`, `uninstall`, and `clean` omit some of those binaries
findings.summary: TOOLS-008: The tools build target produces `indigo_drivers`, `indigo_driver_metadata`, and `indigo_scan_drivers`, but `install`, `uninstall`, and `clean` omit some of those binaries. This can leave stale build artifacts and makes packaging behavior differ from `all`. Decide which helper tools are intentionally private; then either exclude them from `all` or handle them consistently in install/uninstall/clean rules. Next: revalidate historical evidence and assign a scoped repair task; no risk acceptance or closure is implied.

findings.title: SERVER-002: the bundled SHA-1 in indigo_server_tcp.c shifts int values into the sign bit, undefined behavior reported by UBSan on every WebSocket handshake
findings.summary: sha1() promotes unsigned char bytes and the 0x80 padding constant to int and shifts them left by 24 (indigo_server_tcp.c sha1 block loop, tail loop and padding line), which is undefined behavior in C for values >= 0x80. UBSan reports 'left shift of 128 by 24 places cannot be represented in type int' during every handshake in test-server-websocket-sanitize, before and after the FND-000045 fix. Compilers currently produce the expected hash, so there is no observed functional failure. Next action: a scoped fix casting the shifted operands to unsigned, verified by the WebSocket sanitize test running without UBSan reports.
findings.evidence: indigo_libs/indigo_server_tcp.c sha1() (base 48dc893 line 658, line 675 after the task 004 change); UBSan output recorded in 004-fix-websocket-key-overflow/verification.md

findings.title: TEST-011: serial_open_reports_not_a_serial_port expects ENOTTY from /dev/null, macOS 27 returns ENODEV, so make test-unit fails and skips the remaining unit suites
findings.summary: indigo_test/unit/test_uni_io.c:97 asserts the message 'Not a serial port', which needs the OS to fail TIOCEXCL or tcsetattr on /dev/null with ENOTTY. On macOS 27 both fail with ENODEV, which indigo_uni_io.c correctly maps to 'Serial device is not connected'. The test-unit loop exits on the first failing suite, so every run on this host fails and the RAW image suite never runs. Next action: make the expectation platform-independent (for example a regular file or a pty pair where ENOTTY is guaranteed, or accept the documented ENODEV mapping), without weakening the error-message contract.
findings.evidence: 003-initial-repository-audit/verification.md (corrected); 004-fix-websocket-key-overflow/verification.md; probe on macOS 27: open(/dev/null) then TIOCEXCL and tcsetattr fail with errno 19

findings.title: TGT-D29: the aux_upb focuser poll publishes FOCUSER_POSITION and FOCUSER_STEPS OK over a queued request when SI reports no motion
findings.summary: TGT-D29 (alias from the retired indigo_drivers/REVIEW_SWITCH_TARGETS.md): the aux_upb focuser on_timer sets FOCUSER_POSITION and FOCUSER_STEPS OK when SI reports no motion without checking for a queued request. A position request whose handler has not sent the move yet is shown OK, and a FOCUSER_STEPS request that should be refused as overlapping is accepted. Seen as the intermittent focuser_overlapping_request_is_rejected failure (2 of 3 runs on 3.0.0.34, 2 of 9 on 3.0.0.35); still open in driver version 38. Next action: a scoped aux_upb repair task that leaves BUSY focuser properties to their pending handler in the SI branch, with a deterministic regression test.

findings.title: focuser_primaluce sends WiFi SSIDs and passwords into the JSON request without escaping
findings.summary: X_WIFI_AP and X_WIFI_STA insert the client's SSID and password into the request string as is (primalucelib_set_access_point_credentials / _set_station_credentials, formerly inline in the driver). A value containing a double quote or backslash produces an invalid request, which the controller refuses or misreads; the stored-position names already refuse these characters. Found by source audit during the protocol library extraction, which preserved the behaviour on purpose. Next action: a focuser_primaluce task that escapes or refuses such values in the library, with unit and simulator regression tests and a driver version bump.
